title: Trace a check and update that share a boundary
scopeNote: Deterministic in-memory Node.js ESM models contrasting an invariant checked before an interleaving with a check and update performed inside one protected section. They do not prove PostgreSQL isolation behavior. These teaching surfaces are separate from the calibrated assessment cases; stages are optional teaching choices, not a mandatory sequence.

worked_example.teacherNotes: Explain each labeled subgoal. Decisive distinction: a check is only valid for the update that shares its uninterrupted section; a decision made before an await is stale by the time it is applied. Optional principle answer: no. If only the update is locked, both callers still check 100 before either updates, so both pay and the balance is -60. State plainly that the Node model does not establish PostgreSQL behavior; real fixes (FOR UPDATE, conditional UPDATE with affected-row check, constraints, isolation level) need database-specific verification. Showing this example is instruction, not clean retrieval evidence.

completion.teacherNotes: Solution: A:paid, B:paid, decisions:[true,true], balance:-20. Both callers pass the check outside the lock (100 >= 70 and 100 >= 50) before either update runs; the lock then only serializes two already-approved updates, leaving -20. Fix: move the balance check inside the withLock callback so B checks against 30 and returns false (decisions:[true,false], balance:30). Ask for the check-to-update gap reason, not only the trace. Remind the learner this is a Node model, not PostgreSQL evidence. Use completion-solution.mjs to verify; keep this answer key out of the learner prompt.
